content: 1. Flucytosine and tenofovir DF can each increase the toxicity of the other through mechanisms involving nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Flucytosine raises tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Tenofovir DF and flurbiprofen can mutually elevate each other's levels by decreasing renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended due to potential toxicity. 3. Co-administration of tenofovir DF with drugs primarily excreted via glomerular filtration and/or active tubular secretion, such as high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs, may lead to toxicity. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered. 4. Fosphenytoin and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Fosphenytoin increases the levels or effects of doravirine by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Foscarnet and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of doravirine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Co-administration of doravirine with CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Ganciclovir and lamivudine can increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of hematologic toxicity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 10. Fostamatinib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Fostamatinib may also elevate concentrations of BCRP substrate drugs, necessitating dosage adjustments to prevent toxicities. 11. Ganciclovir raises tenofovir DF levels by mechanisms involving reduced renal function or competition for active tubular secretion. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Gentamicin and tenofovir DF both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Gentamicin raises tenofovir DF levels by decreasing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Givinostat increases the levels or effects of lamivudine through mechanisms involving weak OAT2 inhibition. Close monitoring is required, especially with OCT2-sensitive substrates, as small changes in plasma concentrations may lead to serious toxicities. 14. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination may also elevate plasma concentrations of BCRP substrates. 15. Tenofovir DF and ibuprofen can mutually increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended due to potential toxicity. 16. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of doravirine by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Imatinib increases the levels or effects of doravirine by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of doravirine by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Indinavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Indinavir and tenofovir DF also increase this risk. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Tenofovir DF and indomethacin can mutually increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended due to potential toxicity. 20. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of doravirine by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Interferon alfa-2b and lamivudine can increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of liver decompensation. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Istradefylline at 40 mg/day has been shown to increase peak levels and AUC of P-gp substrates in clinical trials. Consider dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates. 23. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of doravirine by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Tenofovir DF and ketoprofen can mutually increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended due to potential toxicity. 25. Tenofovir DF and ketorolac can mutually increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended due to potential toxicity. 26. Lamivudine and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and through unspecified mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of doravirine by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase CYP3A4 substrate levels initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, raising the risk of adverse reactions. 29. Lonafarnib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Lonafarnib, a weak P-gp inhibitor, may require dose reduction of P-gp substrates to prevent serious toxicities. 30. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of doravirine by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of doravirine by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Mavorixafor increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Tenofovir DF and meclofenamate can mutually increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended due to potential toxicity. 34. Tenofovir DF and mefenamic acid can mutually increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended due to potential toxicity. 35. Tenofovir DF and meloxicam can mutually increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended due to potential toxicity. 36. Tenofovir DF increases memantine levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. 37. Tenofovir DF increases metformin levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely due to the increased risk of lactic acidosis. 38. Tenofovir DF increases midodrine levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. 39. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of doravirine by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Mitomycin and tenofovir DF can each increase the toxicity of the other through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Mitomycin raises tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Tenofovir DF increases morphine levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. 42. Tenofovir DF and nabumetone can mutually increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended due to potential toxicity. 43. Tenofovir DF and naproxen can mutually increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended due to potential toxicity. 44. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of doravirine by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of doravirine by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Nelfinavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Nelfinavir and tenofovir DF also increase this risk. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Neomycin PO and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Neomycin PO raises tenofovir DF levels by decreasing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of doravirine by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Lamivudine and nevirapine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Nevirapine and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Orlistat decreases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. The exact mechanism is unclear but may involve a drug-drug interaction that inhibits systemic absorption of the antiretroviral drug. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and if increased viral load is confirmed, discontinue orlistat. 51. Orlistat decreases the levels or effects of lamivudine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. The exact mechanism is unclear but may involve a drug-drug interaction that inhibits systemic absorption of the antiretroviral drug. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and if increased viral load is confirmed, discontinue orlistat. 52. Otesaconazole increases the levels or effects of tenofovir DF through mechanisms involving BCRP inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Use the lowest starting dose of BCRP substrates or consider reducing the dose of BCRP substrates. 53. Peginterferon alfa-2a and lamivudine can increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of liver decompensation. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Oxaliplatin and tenofovir DF both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. This combination may also elevate tenofovir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Tenofovir DF and oxaprozin can mutually increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended due to potential toxicity. 56. Pamidronate increases tenofovir DF levels by reducing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor closely due to the increased risk of nephrotoxicity. 57. Peginterferon alfa-2b and lamivudine can increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an increased risk of liver decompensation. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Pemetrexed and tenofovir DF can mutually increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended.
